sun.name: Sun
sun.blurb: G-type main-sequence star — light-time in this view is not corrected; geometry is for orientation.

mercury.name: Mercury
mercury.blurb: Smallest planet, fastest orbit, extreme day-night swings and no substantial atmosphere.

venus.name: Venus
venus.blurb: Thick CO₂ atmosphere, runaway greenhouse, retrograde spin — brightest planet after the Moon.

earth.name: Earth
earth.blurb: Only known habitable surface — liquid water, active geology, protective magnetic field.

mars.name: Mars
mars.blurb: Rust-colored desert world with polar caps, ancient river beds, and the highest volcano in the Solar System.

jupiter.name: Jupiter
jupiter.blurb: Gas giant and gravitational hub — more mass than all other planets combined; shepherds many small bodies.

saturn.name: Saturn
saturn.blurb: Ringed ice-and-rock giant with a lower mean density than water; hundreds of structured ring features.

uranus.name: Uranus
uranus.blurb: Ice giant on its side — extreme axial tilt produces exotic seasonal lighting at the poles.

neptune.name: Neptune
neptune.blurb: Windiest planet — deep blue methane absorption and a system of faint rings and small moons.

pluto.name: Pluto
pluto.blurb: Kuiper Belt dwarf with a binary companion (Charon) — representative of the third zone of the Solar System.

centauriPrime.l1: Unknown craft, this is Kaelith Harbour Control. We read your drive signature. You are welcome here.
centauriPrime.l2: Hold your course above the cloud line. Our freighters keep the lower lanes.
centauriPrime.l3: Your tanks read low from here. Stay inside the hail and the harbour will pass you fuel, stores and shield charge — no charge to a first visitor.
centauriPrime.l4: Take what you need, traveller. Transmission ends. Safe orbits.

moonPass.title: Lunar low pass
moonPass.fact: The Moon drifts 3.8 cm farther from Earth every year.

earthOrbit.title: Earth orbit

issFlyby.title: Station flyby
issFlyby.fact: The ISS is the size of a football field and weighs 420 tonnes.

marsVisit.title: Mars

venusClouds.title: Venus cloud deck
venusClouds.fact: Venus's clouds are sulphuric acid; the surface below is 465 °C.

mercuryDawn.title: Mercury
mercuryDawn.fact: A day on Mercury lasts 176 Earth days, twice its year.

beltCrossing.title: Asteroid belt
beltCrossing.fact: The whole belt weighs less than 4% of the Moon.

jupiterApproach.title: Jupiter
jupiterApproach.fact: Jupiter has 2.5 times the mass of every other planet combined.

greatRedSpot.title: Great Red Spot
greatRedSpot.fact: A storm wider than Earth, blowing for at least 190 years.

europaScan.title: Europa
europaScan.fact: Under Europa's ice lies an ocean with twice Earth's water.

saturnRings.title: Saturn's rings
saturnRings.fact: The rings are 280,000 km across and mostly under 100 m thick.

titanHaze.title: Titan
titanHaze.fact: Titan has rivers and seas of liquid methane under an orange haze.

uranusTilt.title: Uranus
uranusTilt.fact: Uranus rolls on its side: its axis is tilted 98 degrees.

neptuneWinds.title: Neptune
neptuneWinds.fact: Neptune's winds reach 2,100 km/h, the fastest in the solar system.

plutoHeart.title: Pluto
plutoHeart.fact: Pluto's heart, Sputnik Planitia, is a nitrogen-ice glacier.

solarCorona.title: Solar corona
solarCorona.fact: The corona is over a million degrees, hotter than the surface.

probeFound.title: Deep-space probe
probeFound.fact: Voyager 1 is the most distant human-made object, past 160 AU.

heliopause.title: Heliopause
heliopause.fact: Here the solar wind yields to interstellar space; Voyager 1 crossed it in 2012.

anomaly.title: Anomalous signal
anomaly.fact: Something scanned the ship. Nothing in the catalogue matches.

lightSpeed.title: Light speed
lightSpeed.fact: At c, Alpha Centauri is 4.37 years away. The drive cheats.

alphaCentauri.title: Alpha Centauri
alphaCentauri.fact: The nearest star system: three suns, 4.37 light years out.

centauriPrime.title: Centauri Prime
centauriPrime.fact: An inhabited world. Its harbour control speaks first.

proximaB.title: Proxima b
proximaB.fact: A rocky world in Proxima's habitable zone, found in 2016.

gargantua.title: The black hole
gargantua.fact: In Interstellar, an hour on Miller's planet cost seven years on Earth.

millersPlanet.title: Miller's planet
millersPlanet.fact: So close to the black hole that its tides raise waves a kilometre high.

observed.earth: Earth never sets over Skychaser Base: the near side always faces home.
observed.jupiter: Jupiter turns once in under ten hours — the fastest day of any planet.
observed.saturn: Saturn's rings are mostly water ice, and only tens of metres thick.
observed.mars: Mars has two moons, Phobos and Deimos, both likely captured asteroids.
observed.venus: Venus turns backwards, and one of its days is longer than its year.
observed.m42: The Orion Nebula is a nursery 1,344 light-years off, forming stars now.
observed.m31: Andromeda is 2.5 million light-years away, and closing on us.

firstSteps.title: First Steps
firstSteps.brief: You are down, the lander is cooling, and nobody has walked here. Check the suit, get out to the ridge, take the shot home, and come back in through the airlock.
firstSteps.suit: Check the suit at the lander
firstSteps.earthrise: Frame Earth and take the shot
firstSteps.done: First Steps — the flag is up

power.title: Restore Power
power.brief: The base is dim. The middle array is off the sun and something has cut its feed. Trace it, fetch a coupling from the bench, fit it, and throw the breaker.
power.part: Fetch a coupling from the bench
power.fit: Fit the coupling at the array
power.done: Power restored — the lights are back

telescope.title: Telescope Calibration
telescope.brief: The platform on the western ridge has never been calibrated. Power the mount, align it, and observe whatever is really above the horizon tonight.
telescope.done: First light — the platform is calibrated

comms.title: Comms Failure
comms.brief: Earth has gone quiet. The high-gain dish is off its bearing and its feed is damaged. Inspect it, fit the spare horn, and bring the dish back round to Earth.

expedition.title: Rover Expedition
expedition.brief: There is a crater to the north-west nobody has walked. Charge the rover, drive out, sweep for the sample, bring it back and store it in the lab.
expedition.done: Sample stored — the expedition is home

tips.t1: Light from the Sun takes 8 minutes 20 seconds to reach Earth.
tips.t2: The Moon drifts 3.8 cm farther from Earth every year.
tips.t3: Jupiter's Great Red Spot has been blowing for at least 190 years.
tips.t4: Saturn's rings are mostly water ice; some pieces are the size of a house.
tips.t5: Alpha Centauri is 4.37 light years away — 300,000 years at highway speed.
tips.t6: A day on Venus lasts longer than its year.
tips.t7: Close to a black hole time runs slow: an hour there is years back home.
tips.t8: Proxima Centauri b sits in its star's habitable zone, 4.24 light years from here.

dialog.hello: A pattern of greeting, held long. Roughly: you are new, and you are welcome.
dialog.peace: Both hands open, every band lit slowly. This is what they do when nothing is wrong.
dialog.welcome: They are naming the place. The word for it is the same as the word for the lake.
dialog.suit: They are asking about the suit. They think it is your skin, and that it does not glow.
dialog.star: They are pointing at the star. It has never moved, and they do not understand a sky that turns.
dialog.light: The colours are a question: which is yours? Astra has answered teal, on your behalf.
dialog.water: They are offering water from the lake. It is safe to carry; Astra advises not to drink it.
dialog.friend: That was understood. The whole group answered at once.
dialog.stone: This one wants you to follow. It keeps looking toward the stone.
dialog.gift: They have added a mark to the stone: a suit, standing next to one of them. You are in their record now.

moon.name: The Moon

brief.l1: Good morning, crew. This is Tbilisi. Your first stop is close by: the Moon, about 384,000 km away.
brief.l2: Light gets there in just over a second. The Moon has no air, so no wind or rain ever wears its footprints away.
brief.l3: Land at Skychaser Base, check your suit and take your first steps. We're listening.

obj.land: Fly to the Moon and land at Skychaser Base
obj.firstSteps: Finish First Steps at the base

moon.done: Footprints on the Moon can last for millions of years — there is no wind or rain to wipe them out.

mars.name: Mars

brief.l1: Next stop: Mars, the red planet. Its colour comes from iron in the dust — Mars is, quite literally, rusty.
brief.l2: The air is thin and mostly carbon dioxide, and a day there lasts 24 hours and 37 minutes.
brief.l3: Land at Mars Base, see how the greenhouse feeds the crew, and pick up 3 gems.

obj.land: Fly to Mars and land at Mars Base

mars.done: Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest volcano we know of — about two and a half times as tall as Everest.

venus.name: Venus

brief.l1: Now for Venus. It is nearly Earth's twin in size, but the hottest planet of all: about 464 °C on the ground.
brief.l2: Its thick carbon dioxide air traps the Sun's heat, and the pressure is like being 900 metres under the sea.
brief.l3: Land at the outpost, find out how the cooler keeps the crew alive, then light your jetpack and climb.

obj.land: Fly to Venus and land at the outpost
obj.high: Fly 15 m up on your jetpack

venus.done: Venus spins backwards, and so slowly that one day there lasts longer than its whole year.

mercury.name: Mercury

brief.l1: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the Sun. From its ground the Sun looks up to three times wider than from Earth.
brief.l2: With almost no air to hold the heat, it swings from about 430 °C in sunlight to −180 °C at night.
brief.l3: Land in the Rachmaninoff basin, see how the sun wall shades the outpost, and gather 3 gems.

obj.land: Fly to Mercury and land at the outpost

mercury.done: A year on Mercury is only 88 Earth days — the quickest trip round the Sun of any planet.

jupiter.name: Jupiter

brief.l1: Jupiter is the giant: more than twice as heavy as all the other planets put together.
brief.l2: There is no ground to land on — only clouds of hydrogen and helium, thousands of kilometres deep. Our outpost floats on top.
brief.l3: Set down on the floating deck, learn what keeps it up, then take a jetpack flight over the clouds.

obj.land: Fly to Jupiter and land on the floating outpost
obj.high: Fly 15 m above the deck on your jetpack

jupiter.done: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is a storm wider than the whole Earth, and it has been blowing for centuries.

saturn.name: Saturn

brief.l1: Saturn, the ringed planet. Its rings are ice and rock, from specks of dust to chunks as big as a house.
brief.l2: Saturn is so light for its size that, in a big enough bath, it would float.
brief.l3: Land on the outpost under the rings, check the radio link home, and collect 3 gems.

obj.land: Fly to Saturn and land on the floating outpost

saturn.done: Saturn's main rings are more than 270,000 km across, yet in places only about ten metres thick.

uranus.name: Uranus

brief.l1: Uranus is tipped right over on its side, so it rolls round the Sun like a ball.
brief.l2: That gives each pole about 42 years of daylight, followed by 42 years of night.
brief.l3: Land at the outpost, read how the habitat stays warm at −197 °C, then jetpack up and look around.

obj.land: Fly to Uranus and land on the floating outpost
obj.high: Fly 15 m above the deck on your jetpack

uranus.done: Uranus was the first planet found with a telescope — by William Herschel, in 1781.

neptune.name: Neptune

brief.l1: Neptune is the farthest planet: about 30 times farther from the Sun than Earth is.
brief.l2: Its winds are the fastest in the solar system — more than 2,000 km an hour.
brief.l3: Land at the last outpost, see what keeps its balloons warm, and collect 3 gems. Then come home.

obj.land: Fly to Neptune and land on the floating outpost

neptune.done: Neptune takes 165 Earth years to go once round the Sun: in 2011 it finished its first lap since it was discovered.

earth.name: Home

brief.l1: That's every planet, crew. Time to come home — to Earth, and to Tbilisi.
brief.l2: Earth is the only world we know with seas of liquid water on its surface and air you can breathe.
brief.l3: Land in Tbilisi, step out without a helmet, and take a short walk through the city.

obj.land: Fly home to Earth and land in Tbilisi
obj.walk: Take a 100 m walk through Tbilisi

earth.done: From the Moon to Neptune and back again: you have visited every planet in the solar system.
